title: Robot Arm Inverse Kinematics
prompt:
Create a 3D robot arm with inverse kinematics (IK) using Three.js. The entire application must be in a single HTML file.

## Three.js Import
Use this importmap in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';

## Scene Setup
- Background 0x1a1a2e.
- PerspectiveCamera at (8, 6, 8), looking at (0, 3, 0).
- OrbitControls enabled.
- Ambient light (0x404060), directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) at (5, 10, 5).
- Grid helper at y=0, size 16, divisions 16.

## Robot Arm
- 3-segment planar arm (operates in the XY plane, z=0), mounted on a base at origin.
- Base: cylinder (radius 1, height 0.5) at y=0.25, color 0x666688.
- Joint 0 (shoulder): sphere (radius 0.3) at (0, 0.5, 0), rotation about Z-axis.
- Segment 1 (upper arm): cylinder length 3, color 0x4488cc. Connects joint 0 to joint 1.
- Joint 1 (elbow): sphere (radius 0.25) at end of segment 1.
- Segment 2 (forearm): cylinder length 2.5, color 0x44aa88. Connects joint 1 to joint 2.
- Joint 2 (wrist): sphere (radius 0.2) at end of segment 2.
- Segment 3 (hand): cylinder length 1.5, color 0xcc8844. Connects joint 2 to end-effector.
- End-effector: small red sphere (radius 0.15) at tip.

## IK Solver (CCD — Cyclic Coordinate Descent)
- Target: a draggable green sphere (radius 0.3) that the user can reposition.
- Use CCD IK: iterate from the last joint to the first, rotating each joint so the end-effector moves toward the target.
- Max 10 CCD iterations per frame. Convergence threshold: distance < 0.1.
- Joint angle limits: joint 0 [-180°, 180°], joint 1 [-135°, 135°], joint 2 [-120°, 120°].

## Dragging the Target
- Click and drag the green target sphere on the XY plane (use a Raycaster + Plane intersection).
- The arm follows in real-time.

## Controls
- Press 'R' to reset target to (4, 4, 0) and arm to default pose.
- Press 'W' to toggle workspace boundary visualization (a circle showing reachable radius = 3+2.5+1.5 = 7).
- Slider (id='slider-speed', range 1 to 20, step 1, default 10) for IK iterations per frame.

## HUD (id='hud')
- Joint angles (id='hud-angles'): "θ0: X°, θ1: Y°, θ2: Z°" (integers)
- End-effector position (id='hud-endpos'): "(x, y)" with 2 decimals
- Target position (id='hud-target'): "(x, y)" with 2 decimals
- Distance to target (id='hud-distance'): 3 decimals
- Reachable (id='hud-reachable'): 'Yes' or 'No' (target within workspace?)

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
- `jointAngles`: [number, number, number] (degrees, rounded to 1 decimal)
- `endEffectorPos`: {x, y} (rounded to 3 decimals)
- `targetPos`: {x, y} (rounded to 3 decimals)
- `distanceToTarget`: number (rounded to 4 decimals)
- `isReachable`: boolean
- `ikIterations`: number (current setting)
- `frameCount`: number
- `jointsValid`: boolean (no NaN angles)
- `segmentCount`: number (always 3)

Ensure the animation loop updates __3D_STATE__ every frame before rendering.
physics_constraints: Joint angles must stay within specified limits. End-effector must approach target when target is reachable (distance should decrease over frames). Segment lengths must remain constant (rigid links). No NaN in joint angles or positions. Distance to target must be >= 0. Workspace radius = sum of segment lengths.
